title: Add KMS usage ratecard and residency evidence collector
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: customers and internal compliance teams requested clearer per-tenant KMS billing signals and cryptographically verifiable residency evidence for data residency audits. This PR implements two cooperating pieces: (1) a KMS usage ratecard emitted by the control plane that tags tokenized usage with KMS key identifiers, key-scopes, and billing tiers; (2) a residency evidence collector that accumulates signed residency assertions per request and writes a compact, append-only proof bundle to the audit store. Scope: server-side control plane (api gateway and audit service), small runtime shim to attach KMS-metadata to request envelopes, and an optional background processor that bundles and signs residency evidence for long-term retention. Backwards compatibility: ratecard fields are additive and gated behind feature flag beta.kms.ratecard; the residency collector is opt-in per-tenant via tenant config allow_residency_proofs=true. Design highlights: - KMS ratecard: emits structured labels (kms_key_id, cmk_scope, provider, billing_tier) in the existing usage event schema to avoid schema proliferation. A new mapping layer converts key metadata (from the KMS catalog) into ratecard tiers using a compact rule table. - Residency evidence collector: request-level residency assertions (region_pin, node_zone, key_origin) are bundled with a short canonicalized context and signed by the audit service's attestation key. Bundles are produced in small epochs (5m) and uploaded to the audit store as gzipped ndjson. - Security controls: residency bundles are encrypted-at-rest using the platform CMK and include a Merkle root to enable spot-check proofs without revealing contents. RBAC: introduced two new fine-grained roles: audit.residency.viewer and billing.kms.rate_reader. These map to RBAC v2 attribute rules so operators can grant cross-account read access for audits without granting write or key unwrap rights. Rollout plan: feature-flagged rollout in three stages (canary tenants -> beta customers -> all tenants). Beta tenants will get a telemetry dashboard showing KMS usage attribution to validate ratecard mapping. Tests: unit tests for mapping rules and serialization, integration test that verifies signed bundles validate with the attestation public key, end-to-end test that ensures events with kms metadata flow into billing pipelines. Monitoring and alerts: new dashboard panels for ratecard mismatches and residency bundle upload failures, alert on >1% bundle-signing failures in 1h. Operational notes: - Storage retention default 365 days for proof bundles (configurable per-tenant) - Collector runs with a soft quota; exceeding quota results in sampling with downstream notice - Signing keys are rotated using existing CMK rotation job; old bundles retain verification material. Documentation: added docs pages for the ratecard schema and for how to request residency evidence for audits. Implementation details and migration steps are included below.
